AdjustWalletInput.description:
`POST /wallet/adjust` body: an operator correction. The sign is the
caller's, so the same body covers a store credit and a clawback.

amountCents.description: Signed cents as stored: a credit is positive, a debit negative.

AdjustWalletOutput.description: `POST /wallet/adjust` answer: the balance the correction left behind.

ApiErrorBody.description: The JSON body of every API failure: `code`, a human message, optional data.

ApplyGatewayEventInput.description:
`POST /payments/gateway-events/{gatewayEventId}/apply` body: the id of the
already-persisted event.

CreateOrderInput.description:
`POST /orders` body, exactly the Bun checkout input: the customer, the
lines, the coupon codes typed by the buyer and the chosen method.

code.description: Absent: the server generates a six-character code.

CreateOrderKitItem.description:
One dish the buyer put in a composed kit: which catalog dish, which
variation of it and how many.

CreateOrderLine.description:
One line of a checkout: the catalog ids it names and the price the cart
quoted for it.

kitItems.description:
The composition of a kit the buyer assembles. Absent for a product line
and for a kit whose dishes the catalog locks.

CreateOrderOutput.description:
`POST /orders` answer, exactly the Bun checkout return: the money, both status
axes, the payment window and the coupons that lost.

expiresAt.description: RFC 3339 with milliseconds and a trailing `Z`.

ErrorCode.description:
The eight error codes the TypeScript backend exposed. The wire strings and
their PT-BR messages are verbatim, and are not ours to improve: a client
already switches on them.

ExpireOrderOutput.description: `POST /orders/{code}/expire` answer: the financial axis after the attempt.

GatewayEventOutcome.description:
What applying one event did, the same picklist the Bun contract returns:
`applied`, `ignored`, `rejected` or `missing`.

Health.description:
`{"status":"ok","service":"commerce","timestamp":"<ISO-8601 ms Z>"}`, exactly
the shape the retired endpoint returned.

timestamp.description: RFC 3339 with milliseconds and a trailing Z.

Order.description:
The dashboard's order page: money, both axes, lines, events and the moves the
caller may perform.

OrderAxis.description: Which axis of an order a transition moves.

OrderCodeInput.description:
`GET /orders/{code}`, `POST /orders/{code}/transition` and
`POST /orders/{code}/expire`: an order is addressed by its human code, never
its id.

OrderEvent.description:
One entry of the append-only event trail. `fromValue`/`toValue` hold either a
status slug or a signed-cent amount as text, depending on `type`.

createdAt.description: RFC 3339 with milliseconds and a trailing `Z`.

OrderTransition.description: What the caller may do next on one axis.

OrderTransitions.description: Every move available to the caller at the current pair of statuses.

ProductResponse.description:
The TS contract's `{ product: <detail> | null }` output, which is not a
shared shape: only this read answers it.

PublicKit.description:
A kit as the storefront composes it. `base_cents` is what the card shows:
the charged price for a fixed kit, the floor for a summed one.

available.description: False when the kit cannot reach its own minimums right now.

PublicKitItem.description:
One dish the buyer may put in a kit, with the variation the store locked and
the ones it opened for swapping.

available.description:
False when the chosen variation has no stock left; the dish stays
visible and the composer blocks it.

priceCents.description:
Price of the locked variation; the composer shows it and the sum mode
adds it up.

quantity.description: The locked amount of a `fixed` kit; null for a composed one.

swapVariations.description:
Variations the buyer may pick instead of the locked one, already
limited to what the manager allowed.

PublicMenu.description:
The storefront menu is nested three levels deep: department > category >
subcategory, with the products last. Departments are ordered by name (they
have no `sortOrder` column); categories and subcategories by `sortOrder`,
then name. Inactive levels and empty groups are dropped server-side.

PublicNutrition.description:
A published nutrition label. `published` itself never crosses the wire: only
a complete, intentionally published row reaches the browser. Measures follow
the panel contract: kcal for energy, mg for the rest, thousandths of a
gram/mL for the portion.

PublicProduct.description: One sellable product as the menu renders it. No stock, no cost, no hidden rows.

PublicProductDetail.description:
The direct-URL product adds the label and its own SEO; the menu listing stays
lean, because a card never renders the structured data of its item.

PublicSeo.description:
The resolved SEO of one page: an entity's own override, the store's row and
the store templates behind it.

RecordPaymentOutput.description:
`POST /orders/{code}/payment` answer: the financial axis after the attempt
and the cashback the order's wallet credit is worth.

RejectedCoupon.description: One coupon checkout refused, and why.

TransitionOrderInput.description:
`POST /orders/{code}/transition` body: move one axis to `to`, optionally
saying why. Whether the tuple is legal, and whether the reason is required,
is the state machine's call.

TransitionOrderOutput.description: `POST /orders/{code}/transition` answer: both axes after the move.

Wallet.description:
A customer's wallet: the stored balance and the whole signed ledger behind
it, newest first.

WalletTransaction.description:
One ledger entry. `amountCents` is signed: a credit is positive, a
reserve/spend/reversal negative.

createdAt.description: RFC 3339 with milliseconds and a trailing `Z`.

get.summary: The shape the retired endpoint returned, unchanged.

parameters.description: Id of the already-persisted gateway event.
parameters.name: gatewayEventId
